headline: The battery rail: TALK ME DOWN's back plate gets a real slide tray
lede: The maintenance side of the bomb now hides a puzzle of its own — a seeded three-slot rail whose cells block each other. Read which cell reaches the opening, and only that one comes out. Shipped as one stage of the never-dry run: mechanics, art, autopilot, hash and harness in a single pass.

notes.text: THE BATTERY RAIL (#1917, merged 3051b20): cells sit in a layout keyed on seed+round, the tray opens at the right, blocked or empty slots refuse with the old fiddle silence, and push-back re-clips the cell to the slot it came from.
The rail never moves the module rng: a side-stream keeps every pre-rail bomb byte-identical, so a year of pinned rigs still proves the game — 88 bombcheck gates green unchanged in shape.

New checks must arrive wired: ciscope #1575 demands every aliased check script be scoped or parked, and #1359 demands mutateguard plant/pull around disk mutants. Both went red on this PR before they were right — the audit is the feature.

Prod verification followed the import graph this time: the game chunk isn't in the entry's literal list, and Vercel spent ten minutes serving rotated HTML over 404 assets. Control markers plus chunk-closure sweeps are the honest recipe.
